prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry, and preferred engagement style. I can recommend firms, but to give a useful short list I need to know a few things.

Quick questions
- What are your main goals? (SEO, paid search/ads, social, content, growth/analytics, branding, web/app build, full-service)
- B2B or B2C?
- Monthly budget or annual spend range?
- Company stage and size (startup, SMB, enterprise)?
- Any industry specialization preference (SaaS, e‑commerce, fintech, healthcare, etc.)?

If you want to self-research now, where to look
- Clutch.co and G2 for verified client reviews and ratings
- UpCity and Sortlist for local agency directories
- LinkedIn and Google Reviews for client/employee feedback
- Agency case studies and client lists on their websites

Well-regarded SF-area agencies (examples to consider)
- 3Q Digital — performance marketing and paid media; good for growth/paid search
- Wpromote — full-service digital growth with strong paid/social capabilities
- Jellyfish — global agency with strong analytics and paid media teams
- Single Grain — growth marketing, SEO and paid media (startup & SaaS friendly)
(Verify current office locations and fit — these are examples of types of agencies that operate in SF or nearby.)

How to choose — quick checklist
- Relevant case studies and measurable results (look for KPIs)
- Client references and retention rate
- Experience in your industry / similar customers
- Team structure and who will do the work (senior vs junior)
- Reporting cadence and KPIs they’ll use
- Pricing model (retainer, hourly, performance-based)
- Tools and tech stack (GA4, SEMrush, HubSpot, ad platforms)
- Cultural fit and communication style

If you want, I can:
- Recommend a tailored shortlist of 4–6 San Francisco agencies based on your answers above
- Draft an RFP or a short list of questions to screen agencies
- Pull current top-rated SF agencies from Clutch/G2 and summarize their strengths

Which would you like me to do?
